summary.text: Dingell is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Michigan's 6th District, first elected in 2014 to succeed her husband, John Dingell. Before Congress she spent more than 30 years in the auto industry, including as president of the General Motors Foundation, and chaired the Wayne State University Board of Governors. She serves on the Energy and Commerce and Natural Resources committees.

paragraphs.text: Debbie Dingell was born in Detroit, Michigan, in 1953. She earned a bachelor's degree in foreign service from Georgetown University in 1975 and a master's degree in liberal studies in 1996; her House website lists both degrees as from Georgetown.

She worked for General Motors for more than 30 years, including as president of the GM Foundation and as a senior executive handling public affairs, and chaired the Manufacturing Initiative at the American Automotive Policy Council.
Dingell served on the Wayne State University Board of Governors from 2007 to 2014, and her House website says she chaired the board.

According to her House website, she chaired the Michigan Infant Mortality Task Force, the Children's Leadership Council of Michigan and the Early Childhood Investment Corporation, and is a founder and former chair of the National Women's Health Resource Center and the Children's Inn at the National Institutes of Health.

Dingell won the 2014 election for Michigan's 12th District after her husband, John Dingell, announced his retirement, defeating Republican Terry Bowman with 65.0% of the vote. She has represented the 6th District since redistricting took effect in 2023.
She serves on the House Energy and Commerce Committee and the Natural Resources Committee, and chairs the Great Lakes Task Force.

Her House website cites among her legislative work the HALT Drunk Driving Act, enacted in 2021; the PFAS Action Act, which she led with Rep. Fred Upton; and the Better Care Better Jobs Act, which she authored with Sen. Bob Casey.
According to her House website, Dingell lives in Ann Arbor.
